lead: Joliet plumbing deals with cold winters, basements, older homes and a change in water supply. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Joliet.
risk: frozen pipes, basement backups and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, basement backups and old pipes
why: The Cathedral Area and Upper Bluff have homes from the 1880s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals. Newer subdivisions to the west were built mostly after 1990.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Almost every home has a basement, and heavy rain tests sump pumps and floor drains.
water: Joliet now pumps water from deep wells, which is hard. The city is switching to Lake Michigan water from Chicago because its aquifer is running low.
tips: Add a battery backup to your sump pump.
Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in the Cathedral Area, Upper Bluff, Downtown, West Joliet, the East Side, Cherry Hill and every other Joliet neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Joliet Inspections Division, and plumbers must be licensed by the Illinois Department of Public Health.

faq.q: Is Joliet switching to Lake Michigan water?
faq.a: Yes. Joliet's deep wells are running low, so the city is building a connection to Lake Michigan water from Chicago. The new water will be softer than the current well water.
